_note: Order Up, the phone game at /play (src/play.njk, assets/js/play.js). Everything a non-programmer might want to change is here: the foods, the tickets, the specials, the items and their odds, the family's small talk, and the numbers that set how hard a day is. The rules these follow are in game/README.md. play.11tydata.js checks every `menu` name against menu.json when the site builds and warns if one has gone, so the game can't serve something the café stopped selling.
_note_parts: Every food a plate can hold. `cook` (seconds on the flat-top) makes it a food that cooks: it goes on the griddle first and must be pulled when done. No `cook` and it goes straight on the plate. `sprite` is the drawing in partials/game/sprites.njk (s-<sprite>). `raw` and `raw2` are the colours it shows before it's done. `flip` makes it a food that must be turned half way through (on the levels that have flipping, see `levels`): it stops cooking at the half until it is flipped, and burns if it is left.
_note_bins: The twelve bins, four across, top row first. Bacon, tortilla and cheese keep their place when breakfast turns to lunch at 11am, so a thumb finds them again. The bottom row is the same all day; soup, side and special open at 11am and the roll only with the Cinnamon Roll Case.
_note_recipes: The tickets. `name` is what the ticket says, `menu` the item in menu.json it stands for (left out for something that isn't on the printed menu), `parts` what goes on the plate (four at most; a pickle spear can always be added at lunch for a better tip, so it is never listed), `when` breakfast or lunch, `tier` 1 to 3 (Monday serves tiers 1 and 2; tier 3 comes in from Wednesday), and `photo` the café's own picture for the Recipe Box.
_note_specials: The dawn pick: three of these are offered each morning. All were real specials with their real sides (the weekly posts). One side is a quicker plate; two sides tips more. A special is held hot, so nothing on it cooks: special, then a side for each side named.
_note_catering: Friday's catering order: these platters, one after another, on one clock.
_note_items: Gear and tricks. After close the player picks one of three for free, then may buy from three more; both are dealt by `rarity` using `odds` below. `price` is tips. `max` is how many can be owned (1 when left out). `icon` is a sprite. In `text`, {n} is a number that grows with each one owned: `per` for each, `base` to start from, `unit` how it reads (% , $, s for seconds, times for once/twice); the card shows the number it will be once bought, highlighted, and what it is now (owner 2026-11-12). `kind` is what an item is for: tips (it only earns) or survive (it helps a day through). From `lateShop.fromDay`'s close the shop deals tips items less often, `lateShop.tips` times as likely; the free pick is never shifted (owner 2026-11-13). The tips items were made stronger the same day, so one bought on Monday earns back two to three times its price over a week played to the end (less in a week lost early), and a free one beats the skip bonus through Wednesday; Thursday's shop is half price (`lastShop`), since an item has only Friday left. Prices follow what an item is worth, not its rarity (owner 2026-11-13: rarity is only how often it turns up): from the bot, an item bought on Monday earns back about $1.40 in tips a dollar on Regular, more for the ones that keep a week alive. What each one DOES is in play.js under the same `id`; `text` only says it, so keep the two in step.

_note_odds: The chance of each rarity when a card is dealt (Legendary is never dealt: the Deep Fryer turns up by itself as a fourth card, legendaryChance out of 100 each time the shop is stocked, at a price no week can reach; owner 2026-11-12: it must be a lucky sight, not a regular one). Rares come up more than they used to (owner 2026-11-12), but items only help: the score is the tips a week keeps, so a Rush week won with few items is the best kind, by which close it is (Monday's first). They must add up to 100. A rarity with nothing left to offer falls back to the one below it.
_note_skip: After close the free item can be turned down for tips instead (owner 2026-11-12): `bonus` is the tips by which close it is (Monday's first). More later in the week, when an item has fewer days left to pay for itself. Counted in tips earned, so it adds to the score.
_note_sale: A week that has bought nothing in the shop by `fromDay`'s close (0 = Monday, so 2 = Wednesday's) has `chance` out of 100, at each close from then on, of finding everything `off` percent cheaper (owner 2026-11-12: by Thursday an item has little time left to pay off, and the prices were out of reach). Prices round to $5. Not the Deep Fryer.
_note_finish: Finishing the week pays (2026-11-12, from the bot: a week that bought what it needed and won scored less than one that bought nothing and lost on Thursday). Tips added when Friday's catering goes out on time, by level. The performance bonus is apart from this (`performance`). Counted in tips earned and kept, sent as `finish` with the week.
_note_clean: A flawless day (owner 2026-11-12): no walk-outs, family fed, nothing burnt. `bonus` is the tips it adds, by day (Monday first), counted in that day's tips.
_note_performance: The performance bonus (owner 2026-11-13): paid when Friday's catering goes out on time, said in a banner before the results and listed in them. It is Friday's flawless-day bonus (`clean`, held from 2pm instead of paid then, so a week that fails on the catering never gets it) plus a dollar for every `secondsPerDollar` seconds left on the catering clock (that part was in the catering's own tips before). Counted in tips earned and kept, sent as `perf` with the week.
_note_ranks: At the end of the week each day gets a rarity by its slips (walk-outs, family not fed, food burnt), in the rarity colours: the first line whose `max` it is at or under. Owner 2026-11-12.
_note_achievements: Achievements (owner 2026-11-12): earned once, kept on the phone (localStorage, like the save), listed at the end of the week they were earned and on the Achievements screen; Settings can reset them. `unlocks` names an item that is never dealt until this one is earned. What earns each `id` is in play.js (award). Keep `text` saying exactly what it takes. Each wears the drawing of the item it `unlocks` (owner 2026-11-13); one that unlocks nothing names its own `icon` (a sprite in partials/game/sprites.njk).

_note_trouble: Trouble (owner 2026-11-12: what makes Rush harder instead of only more tickets): some mornings one thing has gone wrong for the day. It is dealt at 6am, said on the morning screen and on the banner, and lasts the shift; never the catering. How often is in `levels` (`trouble`: from which day, 0 = Monday, and the chance out of 100). `share` multiplies how many lunch tickets are the special; `slow` how long the cold spot takes; `chance` out of 100 a ticket is impatient and `speed` how much faster its clock runs; `cost` the tips a burnt food costs; `parts` the foods a No-Show can be (one is out until 11am, and tickets that need it don't come in before then); `after` the seconds burnt food can sit before the inspector fines `fine`; `times` how often the lights go out and `secs` for how long (the flat-top keeps cooking; the tickets can't be read). Each `id` is used in play.js. Owner 2026-11-12: nothing that stops the player outright.

_note_days: How hard each day is. `every`: seconds between tickets. `patience`: multiplies how long a ticket waits. `tier`: the hardest ticket that can come in. `family`: the chance, out of 100, that family comes by at lunch. `burn`: seconds done food lasts before it burns.
_note_tuning: dayLength: seconds a shift takes. breakfastShare: the part of it before 11am. cups: coffees a day. rail: tickets that fit. waitBase + waitPerPart x parts: seconds a ticket waits. lateAt: the share of its time left when a ticket turns red. toGo: chance out of 100 a lunch ticket is to go. luckyBase: chance out of 100 any plate is a lucky one and tips double (owner 2026-11-12; the Lucky Penny adds to it). specialShare: chance out of 100 a lunch ticket is the special; postShare is added for each Facebook Post owned. fair: what keeps a hard day from being an impossible one. A ticket never waits less than cookTimes x its longest cook + perPart seconds a part + base. With bigAtOnce tickets of bigParts parts already up, the next one is a small one. After a walk-out the tickets still up get breath more seconds and nothing new comes for breathHold seconds.
_note_levels: How hard, picked on the title screen and kept for the whole week. `flip`: none (food never needs turning), tap (a tap or a swipe turns it) or swipe (only a swipe does). `wait` multiplies how long every ticket waits, `every` the seconds between tickets (bigger is slower), `burn` how long done food lasts. `family` multiplies each day's family chance in `days` (0 is never); `familyFloor` is a chance out of 100 that applies from Tuesday whatever the day says. `trouble`: from which day (0 = Monday) a morning may bring trouble, and the chance out of 100 it does (see `trouble`). `talk` is how much family says on that level (owner 2026-11-13: on Regular only a few lines): `lines` in all per visit, one every `every` seconds, no more than `maxBubbles` up at once, and with `quietWhenBusy` they hold off while the rail is full or a ticket is late; a level without it uses `family`'s own numbers (Rush). `music` is how far the music may pick up as the shift gets hard, 0 to 1 (owner 2026-11-13: Easy never all the way). The best week is kept for each level by itself.

easy.name: Easy
easy.text: No flipping, no distractions, tickets wait longer.

normal.name: Regular
normal.text: Flip eggs and burgers with a tap. Things get busy by Wednesday.

hard.name: Rush
hard.text: Flip with a swipe. More tickets, and from Tuesday something goes wrong every day.

_note_family: Family at the counter (Wednesday on, see `days`; never on Easy and sooner on Rush, see `levels`). The player is not warned: they just turn up when the week gets hard (owner 2026-11-11). They eat free, they wait a long time, and they talk: a line pops up over the kitchen every `every` seconds and stays until it's tapped. Feed them and they pour you a coffee back (or leave $`leave` if none is spilled); `cookieChance` out of 100 they brought a cookie. Words only, never a face, and no real names. Keep the lines kind: this is somebody's mother.
